svg.text: Cramér–Rao bound: why n·I(θ) and not I(θ)?
In the lessons the bound has n·I(θ), but the formula sheet shows I(θ). Which one do I use for Q1(a)(ii) of
I(θ) is the information in one observation. n independent observations carry n times as much:
So for the whole sample the bound is 1 / (n I(θ)). The formula sheet gives it per observation.
شكراً علي، هذا وضّح لي السؤال تماماً.
نفس الفكرة في ورقة مايو ٢٠٢٢ أيضاً.
